skill.name: draft-my-comments
skill.description: Draft short LinkedIn comments that add a counterexample, extension, specific detail, disagreement, or genuine question without flattery or disguised promotion.
skill.summary: Find a useful contribution to a post, draft a concise comment, or recommend skipping it.
skill.author: prateeks367

security_audit.summary: All seven static findings are false positives: Markdown tool names are not shell execution, and writing advice is not system reconnaissance. The skill explicitly treats posts as untrusted data and prohibits publishing within its workflow. No evidence found of malicious instructions, credential access, or data exfiltration in the reviewed file.

content.user_title: Draft LinkedIn Comments That Add Substance
content.value_statement: Generic agreement leaves little useful information in professional discussions. This skill finds a meaningful contribution and drafts a short comment, or recommends skipping the post.
actual_capabilities: Assess whether a post supports a meaningful contribution and recommend skipping when it does not.
Identify missing context, unsupported assumptions, unexplained reasons, or contrasting experience.
Choose a counterexample, extension, specific detail, honest disagreement, or genuine question.
Draft standalone comments in two to four sentences with the substance first.
Avoid generic praise, disguised advertisements, unsolicited links, and reply bait.
Describe optional VoiceMOAT tools for voice profiles, voice matching, and turning discussion gaps into post ideas.
limitations: Does not publish comments or automate posting.
Does not guarantee visibility, replies, followers, or engagement.
Requires relevant post content and truthful user context for specific claims or personal examples.
Optional VoiceMOAT features require a connected service and a Pro or Enterprise plan; no connector implementation is included.

use_cases.title: Contribute Practical Experience
use_cases.description: Turn a relevant work experience into a concise counterexample or extension of a professional post.

use_cases.title: Discuss Ideas Without Promotion
use_cases.description: Respond to industry discussions with useful context while avoiding product pitches and unsolicited links.

use_cases.title: Ask Focused Questions
use_cases.description: Identify an unresolved assumption and draft a genuine question that advances the discussion.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate One Post
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this LinkedIn post: [post]. Draft a useful two-to-four-sentence comment, or recommend skipping if there is no meaningful contribution.

prompt_templates.title: Add Your Experience
prompt_templates.prompt: Here is the post: [post]. My relevant experience is [experience]. Name the gap and draft a short comment using only these facts.

prompt_templates.title: Develop a Respectful Disagreement
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this post: [post]. My disagreement is [reason]. Identify the assumption involved and draft a standalone comment about the idea, not the person.

prompt_templates.title: Match Your Professional Voice
prompt_templates.prompt: For [post] and [my context], name the gap and choose a comment shape. Draft two to four sentences without promotion. If VoiceMOAT is connected, use get_voice_profile and score_voice_match to check my LinkedIn voice. Do not publish.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: refine a draft with optional connected voice tools.

output_examples.input: Post: Every team should replace meetings with documents. My context: Written updates helped, but unresolved ownership still needed a brief discussion.
output_examples.output: Written updates can replace status meetings, but unclear ownership is a different problem. A brief discussion can resolve responsibility when another document would leave it ambiguous.

output_examples.input: Post: Customer interviews reveal what customers need. I genuinely want to know how the author handles conflicting requests.
output_examples.output: Customer interviews can surface conflicting priorities as well as shared needs. How do you decide which request matters when two customers want opposite changes?

output_examples.input: Post: Our team celebrated its fifth anniversary today. I have no relevant experience, question, or additional context.

best_practices: Provide the original post and relevant, truthful context before drafting.
Name the missing contribution before choosing a comment shape.
Review the draft for accuracy, voice, and relevance before deciding whether to publish it yourself.
anti_patterns: Requesting generic praise or a restatement of the original post.
Disguising a product pitch as a helpful comment or adding an unsolicited link.
Inventing personal experience, numbers, or questions solely to attract a reply.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Will it post comments for me?
faq.answer: No. It drafts text only and explicitly prohibits publishing within the skill.

faq.question: What should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the post and any relevant experience, facts, disagreement, or genuine question you want to contribute.

faq.question: What happens when I have nothing useful to add?
faq.answer: The skill recommends skipping the post instead of producing generic agreement.

faq.question: Do I need VoiceMOAT?
faq.answer: Basic drafting does not require VoiceMOAT. Optional voice tools require a connected VoiceMOAT service with a Pro or Enterprise plan.

faq.question: Does it guarantee engagement?
faq.answer: No. Visibility and replies depend on the post, timing, audience, and author.
